quote.text:
this! codex can create and interact with threads across projects and tasks - all you need to do is ask

I’ve used this recently orchestrate multiple worktrees and implement a feature with different PoVs using subagents

and ofcourse to archive, unarchive and find relevant threads based on context

massive quality of life improvement

replies.name: Praveen Koka
replies.text: @reach_vb 'Codex managing itself' just means delegating your organizational decisions to an AI. Same weight, fewer clicks.

replies.name: avisre
replies.text: @reach_vb "find relevant threads" is basically RAG over your own agent history — if old threads drift out of date, retrieval surfaces stale context. do you prune/expire threads over time, or does Codex handle staleness somehow?

replies.name: Global Perspective 🌐
replies.text: @reach_vb We're getting dangerously close to "just ask" becoming the entire UI.

replies.name: Rohan
replies.text: @reach_vb This is the underrated shift. Once threads, worktrees, and subagents can coordinate, Codex stops feeling like a chat tool and starts feeling like an operating layer for software work. The hard part is making that power legible before it becomes chaos.
